USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

Treating IBS with diarrhea

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 36-year-old woman with established irritable bowel syndrome with diarrhea receives a finite course of rifaximin after appropriate evaluation. Her clinician distinguishes this therapy from medications that mainly reduce motility. Which pharmacologic action best characterizes the prescribed treatment?

  1. Activation of intestinal mu-opioid receptors
  2. Suppression of intestinal bacterial activity
  3. Blockade of enteric muscarinic receptors
  4. Expansion of stool bulk by soluble fiber
  5. Inhibition of intestinal chloride secretion
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Suppression of intestinal bacterial activity

Rifaximin is an antibacterial agent acting predominantly in the intestinal lumen; it is not primarily an antimotility drug.

Understanding the options

Activation of intestinal mu-opioid receptors
This mechanism characterizes antimotility drugs such as loperamide.
Suppression of intestinal bacterial activity
Rifaximin inhibits bacterial transcription and acts mainly within the bowel.
Blockade of enteric muscarinic receptors
Antimuscarinic antispasmodics reduce cholinergic signaling rather than bacterial activity.
Expansion of stool bulk by soluble fiber
Fiber supplements alter stool properties through a physical bulking effect.
Inhibition of intestinal chloride secretion
This is not rifaximin’s antibacterial mechanism.
